screening.reason: Meets inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE I resting-state fMRI connectivity with a heterogeneous graph convolutional attention network for ASD vs control classification.

evidence_spans.text:
This paper carries out research on the challenging public ABIDE I dataset [31], which 
aggregates data from 17 different international collection sites, sharing neuroimaging 
and phenotype data of 1112 subjects. In the experiment, 871 subjects (including 403 
ASD patients and 468 healthy controls) who meet the imaging quality and atypical 
information criteria were used.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was the commonly-used 871-subject ABIDE I subset (403 ASD, 468 HC) meeting imaging-quality and phenotypic-completeness criteria.

evidence_spans.text:
Data preprocessing was performed using the configurable pipeline for the analysis of con- 
nectomes. According to the Harvard-Oxford atlas, there are 111 ROIs in the brain 
[32].
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing used CPAC; functional connectivity used the Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs).

evidence_spans.text: a 10-fold cross-validation schema that mixes data from all 17 sites while keeping
evidence_spans.claim: Primary evaluation was a pooled 10-fold cross-validation mixing all sites in fixed proportion, not a leave-site-out scheme.

evidence_spans.text:
The proposed method is assessed on the autism brain imaging data 
exchange (ABIDE) repository. In total, 871 subjects in the ABIDE I dataset are used 
for the classification task. The best classification accuracy of 82.9% is achieved.
evidence_spans.claim: The proposed HCAN method achieved a best classification accuracy of 82.9% on 871 ABIDE I subjects.

evidence_spans.text:
The proposed HCAN method achieves an average ACC of 82.9%, 
SEN of 76.7%, SPE of 86.6% and AUC of 84.6%.
evidence_spans.claim: 10-fold CV performance: ACC 82.9%, sensitivity 76.7%, specificity 86.6%, AUC 84.6%.

evidence_spans.text:
Availability of data and materials
The datasets analysed during the current study are available from a world-wide multi-site database Autism Brain Imaging 
Data Exchange (ABIDE I) (http://​prepr​ocess​ed-​conne​ctomes-​proje​ct.​org/).
evidence_spans.claim: Data-availability statement points only to the general ABIDE/Preprocessed Connectomes Project resource, not a study-specific participant list or code.

assessments.support: N by diagnosis given (403 ASD/468 HC) with a stated selection basis ("imaging quality and atypical information criteria"), but no specific motion/QC metric or threshold is defined: "871 subjects (including 403 ASD patients and 468 healthy controls) who meet the imaging quality and atypical information criteria were used."
CPAC pipeline and Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs) clearly named, with distance-correlation connectivity described.
ASD/HC labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis, independent of the connectivity-derived predictors.

Primary evaluation pools all 17 sites in a single 10-fold cross-validation preserving site proportions rather than a leave-site-out scheme: "a 10-fold cross-validation schema that mixes data from all 17 sites while keeping"

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort and pipeline/atlas are clearly specified, but the main evaluation is a pooled 10-fold cross-validation across sites rather than leave-site-out, and no leakage-control statement is given for the graph-construction or feature steps.

items.support: N by diagnosis given with a general selection basis, no precise exclusion rule.
No specific motion/QC metric or threshold given.
ASD/HC labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis; diagnostic criteria not restated here.
No leakage-control statement for graph construction or features.
Primary result is pooled 10-fold CV across sites; a supplementary per-site 5-fold CV is also reported.
No study-specific code or participant list; only the general ABIDE resource link.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, a commonly-cited 871-subject subset (403 ASD, 468 HC) from 17 sites.
narrative_row.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs) distance-correlation connectivity structured as a heterogeneous graph; heterogeneous graph convolutional attention network (HCAN) with MLP classification, evaluated with pooled 10-fold cross-validation and supplementary per-site 5-fold cross-validation.
narrative_row.outcomes: Average ACC 82.9%, SEN 76.7%, SPE 86.6%, AUC 84.6% (10-fold CV), exceeding compared methods on the same 871-subject subset; per-site 5-fold CV mean ACC/SEN/SPE/AUC = 75.6%/72.6%/77.3%/83.0%, with performance varying notably by site (e.g. CMU n=11).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No specific motion/QC threshold; primary evaluation pools sites rather than leave-site-out; no leakage-control statement; no study-specific code or participant list.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A graph-neural-network approach on the widely-reused 871-subject ABIDE I subset, directly comparable to several prior published methods on the same subjects.
